mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in RETAIL_REC mobility from t-1w (-16.3) to t-0w (-21.0) indicates a worsening trend in consumer activity that will persist, leading to lower retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks compared to the previous four-week average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the average RETAIL_REC of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed negative trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility, specifically the 1.7 point rise from t-1w to t-0w, indicates a strong shift towards staying at home, which directly reduces discretionary outings and will depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the average RETAIL_REC of the last 14 days, despite the observed increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently low level of WORKPLACES mobility, combined with the sharp decline in TRANSIT mobility at t-0w, indicates a reduced presence of commuters and workers in commercial areas, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to fewer potential customers.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, or if both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recover significantly in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The significant drop in PARKS mobility at t-0w (-11.5 points week-on-week), coupled with declines in other outdoor categories like RETAIL_REC, suggests the onset of adverse weather or new restrictions, which will deter outdoor and discretionary activities, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than the RETAIL_REC value at t-0w, indicating a rapid reversal of the recent decline.

mechanism_narrative: While most mobility categories declined at t-0w, WORKPLACES remained relatively stable (change of +0.2 points week-on-week), suggesting a baseline level of essential work activity. This stability might prevent RETAIL_REC from falling further, leading to a slight positive adjustment or stabilization over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change is less than 1 point week-on-week while RETAIL_REC falls by more than 3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days continues to decline significantly below the t-0w level, indicating that WORKPLACES stability was insufficient to prevent further drops.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility at t-0w (-6.8 points week-on-week), after two weeks of high activity, suggests a reduction in essential errands, which often precedes or accompanies a broader reduction in discretionary spending and retail visits, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days shows an increase or stabilization above the average of the last 14 days, despite the GROCERY_PHARM decline.

mechanism_narrative: The significant single-week drop in RETAIL_REC at t-0w (-4.7 points week-on-week), reaching its lowest point in the observed period, suggests an overreaction or temporary factor. A natural rebound effect is expected as consumers return to previous patterns, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls by more than 4 points week-on-week and is at a 4-week low
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat below the t-0w level over the next 14 days, indicating no rebound effect.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous surge in RESIDENTIAL mobility (+1.7 points week-on-week) and sharp decline in PARKS mobility (-11.5 points week-on-week) at t-0w indicates a strong preference for indoor activities, possibly due to weather or public health concerns, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, or if RESIDENTIAL and PARKS trends reverse significantly in the next two weeks, invalidating the indoor preference hypothesis.
